title: Token-ramped Quant Controller and KV-cohort Fusion to stabilize INT8/FP8 hot paths
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a token-ramped quant controller that dynamically toggles INT8/FP8 kernels per-token based on recent token distribution and confidence heuristics, and a KV-cohort fusion router that aligns KV cache layout and prefetching with the quant controller decisions. The goal is to reduce jitter and tail latency when using mixed INT8/FP8 execution while preserving throughput gains from quantized kernels.

Motivation: In a range of production workloads we observed intermittent latency spikes and quality regressions when the runtime switched kernel paths mid-sequence due to per-layer heuristics. The token-ramped controller smooths transitions by applying a short ramp window (configurable, default 4 tokens) and per-lane confidence scoring so that quant transitions do not thrash the KV cache layout or force repeated dequant/requant cycles.

Key changes (high level):
- token_ramped_quant: new controller that samples recent token logits/scale statistics and emits stable path decisions (int8 | fp8 | fp32-fallback) with a ramp window.
- kv_cohort_router: groups requests into KV cohorts based on quant path to avoid cache layout churn and enable contiguous prefix reuse across similar quant decisions.
- continuous_coalescer: microbatcher improvements to coalesce in-flight requests by cohort, reducing kernel launch overhead without increasing queuing latency.
- Kernel adaptors: lightweight changes in the INT8/FP8 kernel dispatch layer to accept cohort hints and to emit compact metadata for cache stitching.
- Tests and benches: new integration tests for cohort routing and token ramp behavior; updated benchmarks (seq=512/1024) showing improved SLO compliance.

Implementation notes:
- Controller lives in runtime/quant/token_ramp_controller.* and exposes a small policy surface (ramp_window, confidence_threshold, min_stable_tokens). It observes per-token scale estimates from the kernel pipeline and computes a rolling EWMA to avoid noisy flips.
- Cohort router modifies the KV placement algorithm to attach a 2-bit cohort tag to each prefix allocation; this avoids reorganizing large KV blobs when a small subset of requests switch paths.
- Continuous coalescer grouping is best-effort and preserves per-request deadlines; it uses a 200us max aggregation window by default.

Benchmarks: setup: single A100-80GB, 32 vCPU driver, model: open-llm-compatible 7B, seq_len=1024, evenly mixed prompt lengths. Results:
- End-to-end throughput +11% on token-heavy workloads compared to baseline quant path with naive per-layer switching.
- 95th percentile latency reduced from 220ms to 185ms (seq=1024, batch adaptive)
- P50 unchanged +/-2ms.
- Quality (perplexity delta) within noise for <0.5% of datasets; in worst-case prompt families a fallback to fp32 is still triggered by the controller.

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Default policy is conservative; users on Dedicated/Private can enable experimental aggressive ramping via config.
- No schema change to on-disk KV format; cohort tagging is additive metadata that will be ignored by older runtimes.
- Release note recommends enabling on Canary or Dedicated pools before a wide rollout.

Related work: builds on prior quant-path stability efforts (see ENG-2123, PRs that introduced per-layer heuristics) but focuses on end-to-end request-level stability and cache layout effects.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for controller logic
- [x] Integration test for KV-cohort end-to-end path
- [x] Bench harness updated and run
- [x] Docs: short explainer and configuration guide included
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag for safe rollout

discussion:
Ravi Menon (reviewer): The cohort tag sounds useful but adding metadata to KV allocations worries me for space/persistence. Can we make tags ephemeral?
Maya Patel (author): Tags are stored in a side-table kept in-memory by the allocator; durable on-disk KV blobs are not modified. If a process restarts without cohort support the side-table is simply rebuilt from in-flight allocations.
Sofia Alvarez (reviewer): Bench numbers look promising; did you run the A/B on a real multi-tenant Dedicated pool?
Maya Patel: Ran a canary on a 4-node Dedicated pool (internal) — saw similar tail reductions; details in bench logs linked in the PR.
Theo Park (reviewer): The ramp window config seems heat-sensitive. Can we expose an autoscaler to tune ramp_window per-model?
Maya Patel: Added a follow-up item in ENG-2499 to evaluate model-aware auto-tuning; for now ramp_window is per-deployment config.
Ravi Menon: Please add an integration test that simulates rapid quant-flipping sequences (done).
Sofia Alvarez: Approving pending a small nit on controller comments (fixed).
Merge: Squash merged by "Sofia Alvarez" on 2026-03-02.
release_notes: Introduces token-ramped quant controller and KV-cohort fusion to reduce latency spikes when using mixed INT8/FP8 kernels. Default conservative policy; enable via runtime flag in Canary/Dedicated. Improves throughput and 95p latency for quantized workloads.
additional_notes: Follow-ups: ENG-2499 (auto-tune ramp_window), ENG-2530 (cohort-aware multi-region routing), and a perf regression watch in SLO dashboards for the next 2 weeks.
